questions.problem:
Which of the following are affine transformations?

- ${T}_{1}:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}7u-v+6 \\ -7\end{aligned}]$
- ${T}_{2}:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}8v-9u \\ 4u-v\end{aligned}]$
- ${T}_{3}:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}u-5 \\ 8u\end{aligned}]$
questions.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

With this in mind, let's look at each transformation in turn.

- Transformation ${T}_{1}$ is affine. Notice that ${T}_{1}$ can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}7u-v+6 \\ -7\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}7u-v \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -7\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}7 & -1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -7\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}.\end{aligned}
$$

- Transformation ${T}_{2}$ is affine. Notice that ${T}_{2}$ can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}8v-9u \\ 4u-v\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-9u+8v \\ 4u-v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}-9 & 8 \\ 4 & -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}.\end{aligned}
$$

In fact, the transformation ${T}_{2}$ is a linear transformation.

- Transformation ${T}_{3}$ is affine. Notice that ${T}_{3}$ can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}u-5 \\ 8u\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}u \\ 8u\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 8 & 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "${T}_{1},$ ${T}_{2},$ and ${T}_{3}.$"

$$
x=au-2v+b,\,y=4u+cv-2
$$

is shown below. What is the value of $a+b+c?$

$$
[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-6 & -2 \\ 4 & 7\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]
$$

An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

We can carry out the matrix operations using the matrix form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}-6 & -2 \\ 4 & 7\end{aligned}]}}\cdot \overset{u}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}}+\overset{b}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]}} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-6u-2v \\ 4u+7v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-6u-2v+1 \\ 4u+7v-2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding elements, we obtain

$$
x=-6u-2v+1,\,y=4u+7v-2
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+b+c=-6+1+7=2.
$$

\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}4v-u \\ 3v-7\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-u+4v \\ 3v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -7\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}-1 & 4 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -7\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+b+c=-1+4+0=3.
$$

canonical_examples.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $\mathbf T:\mathbb R^2\rightarrow\mathbb R^2$ is a function of the form

$$
\mathbf x = A \mathbf u + \mathbf b,
$$

where $\mathbf x, \mathbf u,$ and $\mathbf b$ are column vectors in $\mathbb R^2,$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

With this in mind, let's look at each transformation in turn.

- Transformation $\mathbf{T}_1$ is affine. Notice that $\mathbf{T}_1$ can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}u+v \\ v-2u+1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}u+v \\ -2u+v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}.\end{aligned}
$$

- Transformation $\mathbf{T}_2$ is affine. Notice that $\mathbf{T}_2$ can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}u-v \\ v-u\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}u-v \\ -u+v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}.\end{aligned}
$$

In fact, the transformation $\mathbf{T}_2$ is a linear transformation.

- Transformation $\mathbf{T}_3$ is not affine since it contains the quadratic term $v^2.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "$\mathbf{T}_1$ and $\mathbf{T}_2$ only."

canonical_examples.problem:
The matrix form of the affine transformation

$$
x = 3u-v + \bbox[Gainsboro,2pt]{a}, \qquad y = u + \bbox[Gainsboro,2pt]{b}v + \bbox[Gainsboro,2pt]{c}
$$

is shown below. What is the value of $a+b+c?$
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072116/assets/43bcde1806155410ba97b0b2e5807d4a0f9cee93ef04f2ccfb413552de74178b.png)
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $\mathbf T:\mathbb R^2\rightarrow\mathbb R^2$ is a function of the form

$$
\mathbf x = A \mathbf u + \mathbf b,
$$

where $\mathbf x, \mathbf u,$ and $\mathbf b$ are column vectors in $\mathbb R^2,$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

We can carry out the matrix operations using the matrix form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ 1 & -5\end{aligned}]}}\cdot \overset{u}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}}+\overset{b}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3u-v \\ u-5v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3u-v+1 \\ u-5v\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding elements, we obtain

$$
x = 3u - v + \bbox[Gainsboro,2pt]{1}, \qquad y = u + (\bbox[Gainsboro,2pt]{-5})v + \bbox[Gainsboro,2pt]{0} \, .
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+b+c = 1+(-5)+0 = -4.
$$
